sections.text: The food which men enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.
The foods that prolong life and increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial and agreeable. These are loved by the Pure.
Those in whom Passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance and disease.

We had been discussing chapter 17, Shraddha Traya Vibhaga Yoga, yoga of three types of faith. We have seen in the last chapter, when Bhagavan ended the chapter, he gave the advice to Arjuna: do everything in life according to the advice given in the scriptures or by the sages. Thats how you will acquire more divine qualities. And these divine qualities are liberating -- they will liberate you from your limitations which are creating sorrows in life.
If you do not follow that, you may incur more negative tendencies which will be more binding. They bind you to this material world. So Bhagavan said that follow the scriptural advice when you decide what to do and what not to do in this world. So obvious question Arjuna had was that what about the people who never had a chance to refer to scriptures? Either by their own choice, that they didnt think it was important, or they never had an opportunity to learn scriptures. And we can imagine in that society, probably the larger mass of people were not allowed to even learn scripture.
Arjuna had a very logical doubt: what happens to all those people? They are working in this world with faith. They have a faith that this is the right way to live life, which will give them happiness. Because at the end of the day, as we have discussed, the goal of life is to be happy. No matter who we are, our goal in life is very simple.
We all want to be happy. If I look at my entire life, it is divided into two pursuits: one is to achieve happiness, and the other is to avoid unhappiness. Bhagavan said we are all working toward the same goal. But those who do not listen to the advice in the scriptures, the books of knowledge, teachers, wise people, ancestors -- they suffer by developing wrong tendencies. Those who follow the advice from the wise people, because theyve gone through that and come to the conclusion this is the right way to act, will benefit from that and acquire the divine, liberating tendencies.
Arjuna said: the people in this world, working in their field, in their life, with faith but having no knowledge of what is prescribed in the scriptures -- as I said, either by choice (they decided its not worth it) or they never had a chance. So what is the nature of their sraddha? They have sraddha too -- that this is where Ill get my happiness in life. Is it Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic? Because if it is just out of my ignorance, one would say that is tamasic. Bhagavan said it is all of the above.
It can be any of the three. If you have not referred to the scriptures but still have faith, your faith can be of any of these three, and at any given time it can be one or another. It is predominantly whatever my personality is -- my faith will be according to my personality. As the faith, so is the person. As the person, so is the faith.
So its a symbiotic relationship. Whichever field I choose to work in, I eventually become an expert in that. I go to architecture school, work in architecture field. More I work in that field, more I get knowledge. More my tendencies become to work in that field. And after about 30 years you become an expert in that field.
At that point somebody says, you made a mistake, Rajan, you should have gone to medical school -- you would have made lots of money. Yeah, Id want to switch overnight but cant do it because my tendencies are now firmly established in the field Ive been working in all my life. Bhagavan says the same thing happens with your shraddha. Whatever shraddha you have, you will continue to pursue that path and have similar experiences. And it will make your shraddha even firmer.
The firmer your shraddha becomes, the more it becomes your nature, your personality. Thats how you can identify or label a person as a Sattvic person, a Rajasic person, or a Tamasic person, depending on the predominant nature of their personality. Bhagavan said their faith can be Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. And then he said that depending on their personality, everything they do will be guided by that faith. The food they eat, the disciplines they practice, the charities they do -- all will be guided by their personality, whether Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic.
And therefore he said, now well discuss in detail what these are. So we have seen the verse: Ahara Tu Api Sarvasya Trividho Bhavati Priyaha. We have to pay attention to the words. Here all hes saying is that ahara, the food, also becomes dear to these people in three different ways. Depending on your personality, your faith, your tendencies, you will like one type of food or another. He did not say that these foods are inherently Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic.
These qualities depend on the mood of your mind. We all know that there are times you like to eat some chatpata, spicy food. And times you really want to stay away from it. Early morning somebody says have idli dosa for breakfast. But we went to the South and there, early morning, the breakfast comes -- idli dosa. And I said, are you serious that you want me to eat idli dosa at this hour?
I thought its lunchtime. No, in the breakfast also idli dosa. So depending on my mood, I like one type of food or another. Yajna, tapah, tatha danam -- not only food is driven by the mood of my mind. These sattvic, rajasic and tamasic qualities are not inherent in the things we see in this world.
Theyre actually the qualities of my mind -- the moods of my mind. That mind will decide whether something is sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic. So depending on my mood, I will decide what I like. Bhagavan said even the food you like will be dependent on the mood of your mind. Whether sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic. Even the efforts you make.
Yajna -- traditionally we call that havan, which we do with fire and put offerings in it. Basically all your life youre doing yajna by putting your efforts, offering your actions in this yajna of your life. That will also be determined by the mood of your mind. The disciplines which you follow -- tapas, austerities -- not just sitting with folded legs. Everything you do to discipline yourself is basically tapas.
If you have to run a marathon, you have to do tapas for that, right? You have to train for that. Thats your tapas. That will be determined by the mood of your mind -- whether sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic.
Where do I make charities when I give something back to society? He says that will also depend on the mood of my mind. Some people will donate toward hospitals and health care. Some toward a sports complex. Whatever you think is dear to your heart, thats where you are going to make charities. Bhagavan said everything in your life will be driven by your faith, your conviction -- whether it is sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic.
Your life will be driven by that. And therefore he said, lets talk about how that affects you. Ayuh sattva bala arogya sukha priti vivardhanah rasyah snigdhah sthira hrdya aharah sattvikapriyah. You really have to be very careful in reading this verse. First of all, it says that if the mood of my mind is sattvic, what do I want to get out of my life? My sattvic mood will say that I want Ayuh -- I want to prolong my life through my efforts.
I want to live a pure life, a long life. Bala, strength -- doesnt mean I want to be like Hercules, but means I dont have to be dependent on others for help. Arogya, health. Health is my real nature. I dont wake up any morning and say, I dont know why Im feeling so good -- let me call my doctor, theres got to be something wrong. Because thats my nature, my real nature. I take it for granted. My health is my nature.
Its when Im not healthy that I notice. Whatever it is, lets take care of it, because its not my real nature. So Bhagavan said sukha, priti -- I want to be comfortable. Nobody wants to be uncomfortable.
I want to choose the food which will make me comfortable. Priti doesnt mean falling in love with somebody. Priti means something that makes me feel good. So I decide what my goal is in eating food first. My goal in eating food is to have ayuh, sattva, bala, arogya, sukha, and priti.
And I want to eat the food which promotes this kind of health. So thats the mood of my sattvic mind. And therefore the food he or she chooses would be rasyah, snigdhah, sthira, hrdya. Snigdhah doesnt mean oily with lots of calories. It means fresh, substantial, has nutritional value. Hrdya means agreeable, which works with my system, which I can digest.
Rasyah, snigdhah, sthira, hrdya. So either Im living to eat, or eating to live, is the question. Here he says the sattvic person will first decide what they want to get out of food. This is the purpose of eating: I want to increase my ayuh, sattva, my purity, my strength, my health, my comfort and my mood. So lets find out which food will be agreeable for me to do that.
And we find that rasyah, snigdhah, sthira, hrdya -- the fresh foods, pure food, healthy food -- are the ones which will give me that. Therefore sattvic people like this type of food. Thats all Bhagavan said here. He did not say eat this or dont eat this, or that people who eat other foods are not good. He said because your goal of life is to increase these types of qualities, you will choose that type of food.
In the next verse he says katva amla lavana atyushna tikshna ruksha vidahinah, ahara rajasasya ishta duhkha shoka amaya pradah. This type of food rajasic people like -- bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, burning. But in the end he says the result would be this. See, in the first verse he said what the sattvic goal is. The sattvic person decided what their goal is first, then chose the food. The rajasic person decided the food I like, thats why Im going to eat it.
Then Bhagavan said the result would be duhkha, shoka, amaya pradah. This food gives you duhkha, discomfort. Anybody who went to a party, had a good dose of hors doeuvres, and then dinner at 10:30 -- tell me, was that the best night you had? It was uncomfortable. Ill tell you what, I didnt sleep well that night.
I wish I had controlled myself. Shoka, grief, and amaya, disease. Katva, amla, lavana, atyushna, tikshna, ruksha, vidahinah -- bitter, sour, salty, extremely hot, pungent, dry, burning. Now Bhagavan didnt say this food is bad. He also did not say dont eat this food.
He said the result of this food will be duhkha, shoka, amaya pradah. These foods will result in discomfort, grief and disease. But he said when Im in a rajasic mood, I dont really have time to think about my food. So whatever is tasty, I will eat that. In a rajasic mode, its not that one group of people only eat this and another group only eat that. When I am in a sattvic mood Ill be very careful about what Im eating. When Im in a rajasic mood Ill say I dont really care -- Im on a one-day trip, whatever.

These verses introduce a fascinating principle: even something as basic as food preference reveals the texture of our mind. Krishna describes how sattvic foods are rasyah snigdhah sthira hrdya - juicy, wholesome, substantial, and pleasing to the heart - and they promote longevity, purity, strength, health, and cheerfulness. Rajasic foods are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, and dry, leading to discomfort, grief, and disease. Notice that Bhagavan does not command eat this, not that - rather, he reveals that our food preferences mirror our mental state, and our food choices reinforce that state.
This week, practice mindful eating as a spiritual discipline. Before each meal, pause and ask: Am I eating to live, or living to eat? Notice your cravings - are you reaching for fresh, nourishing foods that promote vitality (sattvic), or for stimulating comfort foods loaded with spices and calories (rajasic)? When in a hurry, do you grab whatever is available without thought (tamasic)? The teaching here is not about rigid dietary rules, but about using food as a mirror for self-knowledge. Try one meal this week eaten in complete silence, savoring each bite, noticing how different foods affect your energy and mental clarity. Remember: your body is the vehicle for spiritual growth, and how you fuel it reflects - and shapes - your inner state.
